question: Should OpenClaw standardize the narrow `commands list/inspect` contract, the broader cross-registry `catalog` contract, or defer a permanent supported command inventory?
rationale: The alternatives make materially different public naming, inventory, plugin API, Gateway-overlap, and compatibility commitments; repository inspection and implementation quality cannot choose that permanent product boundary.

options.title: Adopt narrow commands
options.body: Standardize command-owned list and exact inspection while deferring ownerless tool adapters, aggregate operator reports, and Gateway convergence.

options.title: Adopt broad catalog
options.body: Own cross-registry inventory plus audit, test-matrix, summary, and the larger plugin metadata compatibility surface.

options.title: Defer core contract
options.body: Keep the RFC and implementation experiments unaccepted until a concrete core consumer and long-term owner justify a permanent surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt narrow commands
recommendation.body: Standardize command-owned list and exact inspection while deferring ownerless tool adapters, aggregate operator reports, and Gateway convergence.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current RFC lifecycle and are the strongest repository-history candidate to coordinate whether and how this draft advances.
